title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.116-118): Grothendieck is building an axiomatics of 'ateliers' and 'magasins', which are material operations (consumption, production) with spatial supports. Σ = Σ_A is a lattice of supports with ∨, ∧ and a disjointness relation f|f' (meaning f∧f' = 0). Elementary spatial figures are families of mutually disjoint supports. On p.116 a family is called 'commutable' (formerly 'admissible'), and Axiom 3 requires that for every chain F_0 ≪ F_1 ≪ … ≪ F_n the corresponding chain of support figures in Figspatdisc(Σ) is commutable.

On this page he tries to build a variant category or poset, Figspatcomm(Σ), of commutable spatial figures. It keeps the same Δ and |·| as before but uses a stronger refinement relation, written ≤_comm: a refinement counts only if the resulting configuration stays commutable.

He immediately sees two problems.
(i) ≤_comm may not be expressible from the structures of the figures R and G alone.
(ii) Even on the structures, ≤_comm need not be transitive.

His test case uses one-edge figures with g ≤ f ≤ e: e = f ∨ f' with f|f', and f = g ∨ g' with g|g', where g, g', f' are mutually disjoint. Then {g, g'} and {g∨g', f'} are commutable, but it does not follow that {g, g', f'} is commutable. Hierarchical, or two-step, commutability does not imply one-step commutability. He concludes 'ça ne semble pas marcher', noting that it works when Σ is a Boolean algebra, i.e. when ∧ distributes over ∨.

In modern terms, 'commutable' behaves like independence of a family in a lattice (each element meets the join of the others in 0), equivalently the family generating a Boolean sublattice with those elements as atoms. The question is whether independence is 'transitive' in the sense of composing along a tree of joins.
errors: Grothendieck's claim that the hierarchical-to-flat implication fails in general is correct for arbitrary (non-modular) lattices; counterexamples exist inside the pentagon N5.

His stated sufficient condition (Σ Boolean, i.e. distributive) is not sharp. The standard lemma that {a,b} independent and {a∨b,c} independent imply {a,b,c} independent already holds in every modular lattice, where independent families also generate Boolean sublattices. So distributivity is more than needed if 'commutable' equals lattice independence. Grothendieck's exact definition of 'commutable' is not on this page, so this is conditional.

ideas.what: Stronger refinement relation ≤_comm on spatial figures, requiring commutability to be preserved, used to define Figspatcomm(Σ)
ideas.modern_name: subposet or subcategory of 'independent' refinements; closest notion is the poset of independent decompositions in a lattice

ideas.what: Observation that commutability of {g,g'} and {g∨g',f'} does not imply commutability of {g,g',f'} without distributivity, so ≤_comm need not be transitive
ideas.modern_name: transitivity (associativity) of independence in lattices; holds in modular lattices (Birkhoff, von Neumann's continuous geometry)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's obstruction is exactly the classical problem of transitivity of independence in lattices. The known fix is modularity, not full distributivity, which suggests his 'commutable figure' axiomatics would work over modular support lattices, such as subspace lattices. This parallels the non-transitivity of compatibility in quantum logic.
missed.quote: il n'est pas clair que ≤_comm soit transitif ! … C'est OK bien sûr quand Σ lui-même est une alg. de Boole, i.e. ∧ est distributif p.r. à ∨
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: it shows Grothendieck brushing against von Neumann–Birkhoff independence theory in a resource/process axiomatics. It would interest someone reconstructing the 1986 'ateliers' project, but it is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a short, abandoned attempt within an idiosyncratic axiomatics. The key observation is a routine lattice-theory fact already known in sharper form (it suffices that Σ be modular).
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'l'axiome Fig 2 et 3 [?] comme (Σ)' should read '… Figspatcomm(Σ). Nous', i.e. commutable spatial figures, continuing p.116's 'Figélspatcomm(Σ)'.
The underset symbol is most likely '≤' with subscript 'comm' (≤_comm), not ≤ with a tilde.
'Mais le seul (connu [?])' is probably 'Mais le seul ennui'.
'et que ≡ [?] sur les structures' is probably 'et que même sur les structures'.
'e = f ∨ f' ou f | f'' should be 'e = f ∨ f' avec f | f'' (disjointness), and likewise 'f = g ∨ g' avec g | g''.
'{g∨g', f'} connus' should be '… commutables'; 'avec [?] g,g',f' mutuellement disjoints' should be followed by 'et donc'.
'il ne s'ensuit [?] pas qu'on [?] résulte que' is probably 'il ne s'ensuit pas (ne résulte pas) que'.
Final sentence: 'C'est [?] bien sûr' is probably '(C'est OK bien sûr quand Σ …)'.
